# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 14
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 14

---

*[PARADISE, CONTINUED. And Peter asks again.]*

1. There also were those who had kept their bodies in purity and virginity, raising their voices in praise to God.

2. I saw those who had suffered for the sake of righteousness. They wore white garments. They had crowns on their heads. Their voices lifted in praise to God.

3. "Where are those who suffered even more than these?" I asked.

4. "God prepared a more glorious place still," the angel said, "for those who preserved the virginity of their body and those who remained pure."

5. There were Abraham and Isaac and Jacob — all three of them — in a state of tremendous joy.

6. Above them: the angels of light, and above them the seraphim, and all around a vast multitude of the righteous, bathed in a great white light.

7. I was overwhelmed with wonder and joy. "What is this place?" I asked. "And who are all these people?"

8. "This place was made for those who suffered for God," the angel said, "and for those who feared him."

9. Then I turned to the Lord. "Lord," I said, "is there truly no possibility of mercy for sinners at the last? For it is written that you are compassionate and merciful — that you take no pleasure in the death of a sinner."

10. The Lord looked at me. "Listen, Peter," he said. "What I have told you, what you have seen and heard — it is true. No one who sins and dies in sin will be saved.

11. But there will be mercy for some. And some will not be saved — they will go to the place of punishment forever.

12. Those I have received from below — those I have delivered — they will find mercy through me."

---
*PNEUMA note: The three patriarchs (v.5) and the layered celestial hierarchy (angels → seraphim, v.6) give the paradise a cosmic depth. Peter's second intercession (v.9) shows him still pressing, still unable to accept what he has seen. The Lord's answer (vv.10–12) remains the most theologically complex in the entire APE — judgment is real, mercy is real, and the mystery of who is delivered is kept in God's hands alone.*
